outOfScope: market sizing or statistically representative sampling
individualized legal or privacy compliance advice

claims.claim: In-depth interviews are suited to learning about current or likely users' experiences and should use a discussion guide with open, neutral questions and follow-up prompts that elicit real examples.
Recruitment should be tied to the people and user groups relevant to the research question, while protecting participant details and including relevant differences in access needs or experience.

A small interview round can reveal patterns and generate questions, but it is not a statistically representative estimate of a market; surveys and similar quantitative methods need substantially more participants for clear findings.

For user research, informed consent should cover participation, the purpose and activities, the data collected, recordings, intended uses and sharing, voluntariness, withdrawal, and retention; requirements depend on jurisdiction and context.

Participant information and research materials should be limited to what is needed, stored and shared carefully, and de-identified where appropriate; collecting and keeping data can create privacy obligations that vary by jurisdiction.
Analysis should distinguish what a participant said or did from the team's interpretation, then sort observations into themes before writing bounded findings and next questions.
Open-ended questions give an interview participant room to speak freely rather than requiring a yes-or-no response.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft supplied only generic boilerplate, three-option questions, no consent or privacy guidance, no discussion of qualitative sampling limits, and no verifiable sources.
correctionsNeeded: Replaced the generic definition with a bounded explanation of interview planning, moderation, data handling, and note analysis.
Added the limit that a small purposive interview set can inform questions and patterns but does not estimate prevalence or market size.
Added informed, voluntary participation, recording permission, data minimization, and jurisdiction-qualified privacy cautions.
Added exactly five four-option questions with independently checked keys distributed A, B, C, D, A.
rightsIssues: GOV.UK guidance and the OpenStax page were used as reference-only sources. No source prose or proprietary interview template was reproduced.
Privacy and consent guidance is presented as an ethical method and general education, not as jurisdiction-specific legal advice.

sourceRecords.title: Using in-depth interviews
sourceRecords.notes: Read live. Supports recruiting current or likely users, using open and neutral questions, following up for detail, covering consistent topics, and focusing on stories and real examples rather than generalities. Original synthesis only.

sourceRecords.title: Finding participants for user research
sourceRecords.notes: Read live. Supports tying recruitment to actual or likely users, considering different access needs, using only the participant information needed, limiting access to it, and deleting it when no longer needed. Original synthesis only.

sourceRecords.title: Plan user research for your service
sourceRecords.notes: Read live. Supports setting research questions and relevant user groups; describes typical small rounds for in-depth interviews and contrasts them with methods such as surveys that need hundreds of participants for clear findings. The lesson does not treat its suggested numbers as a universal rule. Original synthesis only.

sourceRecords.title: Getting informed consent for user research
sourceRecords.notes: Read live. Supports explaining who conducts the research, purpose, data, activities, uses and sharing, recording or observation, voluntariness and withdrawal, retention, and accessible evidence of consent. The lesson makes no claim that UK requirements govern other jurisdictions. Original synthesis only.

sourceRecords.title: Managing user research data and participant privacy
sourceRecords.notes: Read live. Supports clear early disclosure, collecting the minimum needed to manage participation, secure limited sharing, deletion when no longer needed, and using data within the stated consent. Original synthesis only.

sourceRecords.title: Taking notes and recording user research sessions
sourceRecords.notes: Read live. Supports detailed records, notes based on observations rather than interpretations, recording consent, secure storage, and removing personal or confidential details when appropriate. Original synthesis only.

sourceRecords.title: Analyse a research session
sourceRecords.notes: Read live. Supports promptly extracting observations, recording what was said or done rather than interpretation, grouping observations into themes, forming findings, and identifying next actions or questions. Original synthesis only.

sourceRecords.title: Writing Guide with Handbook, 15.5 Writing Process: Thinking Critically About How People and Language Interact
sourceRecords.notes: Read live. Supports the general research-method point that open-ended interview questions avoid yes-or-no answers and let participants speak freely. Original synthesis only.
